issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to initialize the SealSaloon attributes (including the Stock) in the instance constructor (lines referencing initialization in constructor), but also requires that the stock attribute be static/shared across all instances. Initializing a static final field in an instance constructor is contradictory and not valid Java; this conflict will confuse students about where and how to initialize the shared stock.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify and make consistent whether 'stock' is an instance field or a static field. If stock must be shared (static final), update the problem statement to instruct students to initialize it at declaration or in a static initializer (not in the instance constructor). Alternatively, remove the requirement that stock be static so it can be initialized in the constructor. Ensure the description matches the intended solution (static final initialized at declaration).

issues.description: Template Stock.getStockIngredients() returns a List<StockIngredient> (template), but the solution's Stock.getStockIngredients() returns a StockIngredient[] array. This change in method return type between template and solution is a structural mismatch that could confuse students about the expected getter signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the getter signature consistent across template and solution. Either keep getStockIngredients() returning a List<StockIngredient> in both places, or have it return a StockIngredient[] in both. Update the template (and problem description if necessary) so students implement with the consistent return type expected by tests and examples.
